Here’s a concise, safe‑first guide you can follow:

| Step | Action | Why It Matters |
|------|--------|----------------|
| **1** | **Unlock the driver’s door** – Use your key fob or manual key. | You need access to the ignition or start button. |
| **2** | **Engage the parking brake** – If it’s already engaged, double‑check it’s fully locked. | Prevents accidental movement while the engine runs. |
| **3** | **Start the engine** – Turn the key to “ON” or press the start/stop button (if your car has one). | Allows you to read gauges and run diagnostics. |
| **4** | **Check the fuel gauge** – Look at the dashboard indicator or use an OBD‑II scanner if you have one. | Ensures you know how much fuel remains before driving. |
| **5** | **Verify battery health** – Inspect the battery compartment for corrosion, check the voltage with a multimeter (12 V is normal), or use a diagnostic tool. | A healthy battery prevents unexpected shutdowns. |
| **6** | **Monitor engine temperature** – Keep an eye on the coolant gauge or temperature sensor reading. | Overheating can damage components. |
| **7** | **Turn off the engine when finished** – Switch the ignition to “OFF” or press the stop button. | Saves fuel and protects the battery. |

### Quick Tips

- **Safety First:** Make sure the car is parked on a flat surface and the gear selector is in “P” (or “N”) before starting.
- **Use a Diagnostic Scan Tool:** If you have an OBD‑II reader, plug it into the port under the dash to pull real‑time data on fuel consumption, battery voltage, and error codes.
- **Keep a Log:** Write down the fuel level and battery voltage each time you start the engine. Over time, this helps spot trends or potential issues early.

If you’re unsure about any part of the process—especially if your vehicle has a push‑button start or a keyless entry system—consult the owner’s manual or contact the dealership for guidance.
